reviews.summary: Recent QNT/USDC spot-pair removals at Binance and Bitrue create venue-specific liquidity/route-fragmentation risk. This does not establish a QNT-EUR halt or a protocol/security failure, but is directly relevant to execution conditions around QNT.
materialRisks: Binance removed QNT/USDC on September 18, 2026, citing its periodic trading-pair review; QNT remained available through other pairs. ([binance.com](https://www.binance.com/en-AE/support/announcement/detail/30b1347d97324180bb469c761e4eed5a?utm_source=openai))

Bitrue also delisted QNT/USDC on September 17, 2026. Multiple recent removals of the same QNT pair can concentrate liquidity and worsen cross-venue execution resilience. ([support.bitrue.com](https://support.bitrue.com/hc/en-001/articles/62341783980697-Delisting-of-Spot-Trading-Pair-September-17-2026?utm_source=openai))

facts.fact: Quant announced on September 24, 2026 that The Clearing House selected its technology for an on-chain-money initiative; Quant’s own materials state the network is expected to open to participating institutions in the first half of 2027, so the announcement is not evidence of immediate live usage. ([quant.network](https://quant.network/press-releases/the-clearing-house-partners-with-quant-to-advance-the-on-chain-money-initiative/?utm_source=openai))
No fresh primary-source evidence found of a QNT token exploit, Quant protocol outage, supply unlock, or regulatory action directly impairing QNT during the review window.

Kraken’s recent status history shows an Ethereum ERC-20 deposit-delay incident on September 26, 2026, with a fix implemented; the available status result does not identify QNT specifically or show a current QNT-EUR trading halt. ([status.kraken.com](https://status.kraken.com/history?utm_source=openai))
